paragraphs.text: Vulgo dicitur, saith the Vulgate; Dicendo dicitur, say others. They say, and they say well, for they have good law for it. {Deu 24:4} But I am above law, saith God, and will deal with thee, not according to mine ordinary rule, but according to my prerogative. Thou shalt be a paradox to the Bible; for I will do that in favour of thee, which I have inhibited others in like case to do, and that scarce any man would do, though there were no law to inhibit it, as one here paraphraseth.
paragraphs.anchor: They say.

paragraphs.text: Great sins do greatly pollute, that of adultery especially, for this is a heinous crime; yea, it is an iniquity to be punished by the judges. {Job 31:11}
paragraphs.anchor: Shall not the land be greatly polluted?

paragraphs.text: Haec est Dei clementia insuperabilis; God’s mercy is matchless. No man, no god, would show mercy as he doth. {Mic 7:18 Mal 3:7 Zec 1:3} He followeth after those that run from him, as the sunbeams do the passenger that goeth from them; and as it is sweetly set forth by our Saviour in those three parables of the lost coin, the lost sheep, and the lost son. {Luk 15:3-32} Paul alloweth of Mark, {2Ti 4:11} though before he had refused him, {Act 15:38} and willeth others to entertain him. {Col 4:10-11} Let none despair that hath but a mind to return to God, from whom he hath deeply revolted.
paragraphs.anchor: But thou hast played the harlot; yet return to me.

paragraphs.text: There is a natural Novatianism in the timorous conscience of convinced sinners, to doubt and question pardon for sins of apostasy and falling after repentance. But this need not be, we see here. Pernicious was Ahithophel’s counsel to Absalom, "Go in to thy father’s concubines"; this he judged such an injury as David would never put up; yet "return again to me, saith the Lord," and all shall be well between us.
Pouring out thy spiritual whoredoms, as Papists now do with their crosses, chapels, pictures, set up in all places.
paragraphs.anchor: And see where thou hast not been lien with.

paragraphs.text: For thy customers and copse mates, like a common strumpet. See Gen 38:19 Eze 16:24-25; Eze 16:31.
paragraphs.anchor: In the ways thou hast sat for them.

paragraphs.text: As highway robbers wait for and waylay passengers, making it thy trade.
paragraphs.anchor: As the Arabian in the wilderness.

paragraphs.text: Drought and dearth have ensued upon thy sin. By showers here understand the former rain, called also the seeds’ rain. {Isa 30:23}
paragraphs.anchor: Therefore the showers have been withholden.

paragraphs.text: That commonly came a little before harvest, and was much desired.
paragraphs.anchor: And there hath been no latter rain.

paragraphs.text: And thou hadst a whore’s forehead.] Quam pudet non esse impudentem; { a} that can blush no more than a sackbut. We have heard, saith a reverend writer, of virgins, which at first seemed modest, blushing at the motions of an honest love, who, being once corrupt and debauched, have grown flexible to easy entreaties to unchastity, and from thence boldly lascivious, so as to solicit others, so as to prostitute themselves to all comers, yea, as the casuists complain of some Spanish brothels, {b} to an unnatural filthiness. The modest beginnings of sin will make way for immodest proceedings. Let men take heed of that αδιατρεψια, i.e., inverecundia, shamelessness, that Caligula liked so well in himself, and that the heretics, called Effrontes, professed. It is a hard thing to have a brazen face and a broken heart.
{a} Augustine.
{b} Dr Hall’s Remedy of Profan., p. 179.
And is not this extreme impudence? Hast thou a face thus to collogue? Hypocritis nihil impudentius; hypocrites are impudent flatterers; they would, if they could, cheat God of his heaven.
paragraphs.anchor: Wilt thou not from this time cry unto me?

paragraphs.text: i.e., My dear husband. {Pro 2:17} Fair words are light cheap, and may make fools fain; but God is not to be so courted and complimented.
paragraphs.anchor: Thou art the guide of my youth

paragraphs.text: Will he not? {Nah 1:2} and is there not good reason he should do so, so long as you speak and do evil things as you can, obstinately persisting in thy sinful practices? He that repenteth with a contradiction, saith Tertullian, God will pardon him with a contradiction. Thou repentest, and yet continuest in thy sins. God will pardon thee, and yet send thee to hell: there is a pardon with a contradiction.
paragraphs.anchor: Will he reserve his anyer for ever?

paragraphs.text: i.e., To thine utmost. Nolunt solita peccare, saith Seneca of some; they strive to outsin themselves and others.
paragraphs.anchor: As thou couldst

paragraphs.text: This is the beginning of a new sermon, as most hold. Josiah was a religious prince, and a zealous reformer; and hypocrisy reigned exceedingly in his days, as we see here: and as holy Bradford in his letters complaineth that it did likewise in King Edward VI’s days, who was our English Josiah, among the great ones especially, who were very corrupt.
paragraphs.anchor: The Lord also said unto me in the days of Josiah.

paragraphs.text: sc., Ever since Solomon’s mind began to be corrupted, {1Ki 11:4} and now she smarteth for it; yet is not Judah warned by her example.
paragraphs.anchor: She is gone up upon every high mountain

paragraphs.text: Or, Yet I said; but I lost my sweet words upon her.
paragraphs.anchor: And I said after she had done.

paragraphs.text: That which others could not so easily discern - viz., their hypocrisy and hollow heartedness, their incorrigibleness also, and refusing to be warned by what had befallen their brethren. God looked that Israel’s corrections should have been Jerusalem’s instructions, and that by their lashes she should have been lessoned, which because she was not he is highly displeased, and speaks of it here in a very angry dialect.
paragraphs.anchor: And I saw.

paragraphs.text: But slighted the kindness of such a caution, and despised the counsel that was written to her in her sister’s blood.
paragraphs.anchor: Yet her treacherous sister Judah feared not.

paragraphs.text: Being therefore the worse, because she should have been the better of the two.
paragraphs.anchor: But went and played the harlot also.

paragraphs.text: Or, better, Through the vocalness of it; the loudness of her lewdness. Heb., the voice or noise of her whoredom, the fame and bruit of it, for it is spoken of far and near.
paragraphs.anchor: And it came to pass through the lightness of her whoredom.

paragraphs.text: Haec fere omnia in caecum, erroneum, meretriciumque Papatum apte hodie torqueri possunt. Do not idolatrous Papists even the same?
paragraphs.anchor: And committed adultery with stones and with stocks.

paragraphs.text: Josiah did, but the people did not, as soon appeared, when in the next king’s reign they fell off as fast as leaves do in autumn. And so they did here, when Queen Mary set up Popery.
paragraphs.anchor: Hath not turned unto me with her whole heart.

paragraphs.text: That is, she is less guilty and faulty of the two; because Judah sinned against more means and mercies, and because she received not instruction by her sister’s destruction; therefore shall she feel what she feared not at a distance; therefore shall she taste of Israel’s rod because she would not hear it; she that would not tremble at her sister’s divorce, must herself be divorced, and be judged as "women that break wedlock," {Eze 16:38} "bearing her own shame for her sins that she had committed, more abominable than theirs." {Eze 16:52}
paragraphs.anchor: The backsliding Israel hath justified herself.

paragraphs.text: i.e., Toward Assyria and Media, into which countries the ten tribes had been carried captive. And although they cannot hear thee, yet in time this prophecy may be brought to their hearing; and the men of Judah, meanwhile, may be wrought upon thereby.
paragraphs.anchor: Go and proclaim these words toward the north

paragraphs.text: Heb., I will not make my face to fall: I will not further frown upon you, or deal hardly with you.
paragraphs.anchor: And I will not cause mine anger to fall upon you.

paragraphs.text: Heb., I will not keep for ever. There is nothing that a man is more ready to keep than his wrath. Therefore the Hebrews put keep, for keep wrath. {Psa 103:9 Lev 19:18 Jer 3:5}
paragraphs.anchor: I will not keep anger for ever.

paragraphs.text: Thus favour is promised to the ten captivated tribes, sed per modulum unius paenitentiae, but upon condition of their true repentance, one part whereof is confession of sin. {Pro 28:13 Psa 32:4} When thy sins and God’s wrath meeting in thy conscience, saith one, make thee deadly sick, then pour forth thy soul in confession; and as it will ease thee, as vomiting useth to do, so also it will move God to pity, and to give thee cordials and comforts to restore thee again. {a}
paragraphs.anchor: Only acknowledge thine iniquity.

paragraphs.text: {a} Facit peccator confitendo propitium, quem non facit negando nescium. - August.
See on Zec 1:3.
paragraphs.anchor: Turn, O backsliding children.

paragraphs.text: And, as "I hate putting away," {Mal 2:16} so I can receive to favour a wife that hath been disloyal, {Jer 3:1} and after a divorce.
paragraphs.anchor: For I am married unto you.

paragraphs.text: i.e., Though but a few, {Isa 10:11-12; Isa 17:6; Isa 24:3} all the rest hardening their hearts by unbelief. This hath been principally fulfilled in the days of the gospel.
paragraphs.anchor: And I will take you one of a city

paragraphs.text: God gives faithful pastors oft for the sake of but a few that are there to be converted: Et vilissimus pagus est palatium eburneum, in quo est pastor et credentes aliqui, saith Luther, {a} The poorest village is an ivory palace, if there be but in it a pastor and some few believers. Such pastors as God here promiseth (and more largely describeth, Jer 23:1-40 Eze 34:1-31), are special gifts of God: "I will give you pastors." David, after he had discomfited the Amalekites, sent gifts to his friends in Judah. {1Sa 30:26} Great Alexander, when he had prevailed at the river Granicus, and was now ascended into the upper parts of Asia, sent back many gifts to assure them of his love in Macedonia.
paragraphs.anchor: And I will give you pastors according to my heart.

paragraphs.text: The like doth God to his Church by sending them pastors, with such two adjuncts as are here - (1.) Adherent, his own approbation; (2.) Inherent, skill to teach the people. See Eph 4:8. {See Trapp on "Eph 4:8"}
{a} Luth., tom. iii. p. 81.
When the gospel shall be preached, the ancient ceremonies shall be abolished. {a} This was not so easily believed, and is therefore here again and again assured.
paragraphs.anchor: They shall say no more, The ark, &c.

paragraphs.text: {a} Paulus ea vocat stercora et rudera.
i.e., The Church Christian.
paragraphs.anchor: They shall call Jerusalem

paragraphs.text: The throne of glory; {Jer 4:2} so Exo 17:16, because the hand upon the throne of the Lord - that is, say some, Amalek’s hand upon the Church, which is elsewhere also called the temple of God.
paragraphs.anchor: The throne of the Lord.

paragraphs.text: i.e., Not at random, but by rule. {Eph 5:15} Heb., Not any more after the sight of their heart - i.e., as themselves thought good, but as God directeth them.
paragraphs.anchor: Neither shall they walk any more, &c.

paragraphs.text: All the elect shall be reunited in Christ; unless we shall understand it of the last reduction of the nation into one. {Isa 11:13 Eze 37:16; Eze 37:22 Hos 1:11}
paragraphs.anchor: In that day shall the house of Judah walk with the house of Israel.

paragraphs.text: i.e., Out of the place of their captivity, whereby was figured our spiritual captivity, &c.
paragraphs.anchor: And they shall come together out of the land of the north

paragraphs.text: How, but by my free grace alone, since thou hast so little deserved it? For the causes of our adoption, see Eph 1:5-6.
paragraphs.anchor: But I said, How shall I put thee among the children?

paragraphs.text: The heavenly Canaan, which is here fitly called "a land of desire" or "delight," a heritage or possession of godliness, a land of the hosts or desires of the nations.
paragraphs.anchor: And give thee a pleasant land.

paragraphs.text: And My Father, affectionately uttered, is an effectual prayer. Ah! Pater brevissima quidem vox est, sed omnia complectitur, saith Luther - i.e., Ah! Father is but a little word, but very comprehensive; it is such a piece of eloquence as far exceedeth the rollings of Demosthenes, Cicero, or whatsoever most excellent orator.
paragraphs.anchor: And I said, Thou shall call me, My Father.

paragraphs.text: This ye have done, but that is your present grief, and now you look upon your former disloyalties with a lively hatred of them, holding that the time past of your life may suffice to have wrought the will of the Gentiles, &c. {1Pe 4:3}
paragraphs.anchor: Surely as a treacherous wife, &c.

paragraphs.text: Where they were wont to worship idols, now they weep for their sins, and pray for pardon.
paragraphs.anchor: A voice was heard upon the high places.

paragraphs.text: This is it that now draweth from them prayers and tears. See Jer 31:18 Lam 5:14. Oi nalanu, chi chattanu. Woe worth us that ever we thus sinned. Some understand those words, "A voice is heard," as showing God’s readiness to hear penitent sinners as soon as they begin to turn to him, even before they speak, as the father of the prodigal met him, &c.
paragraphs.anchor: For they have perverted their ways.

paragraphs.text: Give the whole turn, and not the half turn only. So Act 2:38, Peter said to them that were already pricked at heart, "Repent ye," even to a transmentation; and Jer 3:19, "Repent ye, and be converted, that your sins may be blotted out." Repent not only for sin, but from sin too; be thorough in your repentance; let it be such as shall never be repented of. {2Co 7:10} It is not a slight sorrow that will serve apostates’ turn; it must be deep and downright.
paragraphs.anchor: Return, ye backsliding children.

paragraphs.text: Pardon your sins, and heal your natures. "I will love you freely," and cause your broken bones to rejoice. {Hos 14:4 Isa 19:22} Oh sweetest promise! What wonder, then, that their hard hearts were forthwith melted by it into such a gracious compliance as followeth.
paragraphs.anchor: And I will heal your backslidings.

paragraphs.text: See Zec 13:9. {See Trapp on "Zec 13:9"}
paragraphs.anchor: Behold, we come to thee.

paragraphs.text: Heb., Truly in vain from the hills, the multitude, the mountains: it is like to that in Hos 14:3, "Asshur shall not save us; neither will we say any more to the works of our hands, Ye are our gods." {See Trapp on "Hos 14:3"}
paragraphs.anchor: Truly in vain is salvation hoped for from the hills.

paragraphs.text: They trust not God at all that trust not God alone.
paragraphs.anchor: Truly in the Lord our God.

paragraphs.text: That shameful thing, Baal hath done it; {Jer 11:13 Hos 9:10} he hath even eaten up our cattle and our children, of whom, if any be left, yet there is nothing left for them. And this we now see, long and last, paenitentia ducti, et nostro male edocti, having bought our wit, and paid dear for our learning. And may not many ill husbands among us say as much of their drunkenness and wantonness? See Pro 5:9-12. {See Trapp on "Pro 5:9"} {See Trapp on "Pro 5:10"} {See Trapp on "Pro 5:11"} {See Trapp on "Pro 5:12"}
paragraphs.anchor: For shame hath devoured the labour of our fathers.

paragraphs.text: We that once had a whore’s forehead, {Jer 3:3} and seemed past grace, are now sore ashamed of former miscarriages, yea, our confusion covereth us, {as Psa 44:15} because "we have sinned against the Lord our God, we and our fathers, from our youth unto this day, and have not obeyed the voice of our God." Lo, here a dainty form and pattern of penitent confession, such as is sure to find mercy. Haec sane omni tempore Christiana est satisfactio, non meritoria aliqua Papistica atque nugivendula. {a} Only we must not acknowledge sin with dry eyes, but point every sin with a tear, &c.
paragraphs.anchor: We lie down in our shame.

paragraphs.text: {a} Zegedin.
